original_question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold of dimension >= 3 admit a closed geodesic net whose underlying graph is a theta-graph, namely a graph with two vertices joined by three distinct edges?
target_in_paper: Section 2, Problem 2.0.3: "Is it true that each closed Riemannian manifold of dimension ≥ 3 has a θ-graph shaped closed geodesic net?" ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1904.00483))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right ambient object (a closed Riemannian manifold), the correct dimension threshold (≥ 3), the correct existence quantifier (every), and the correct graph shape (the θ-graph, i.e. two vertices joined by three distinct edges). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1904.00483))
missing_details: The paper phrases the problem as asking for a "θ-graph shaped closed geodesic net," i.e. a closed geodesic net modeled on the θ-graph; using the paper's modeling language makes the question closer to the official formulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1904.00483))

To make the question stand-alone, "closed geodesic net" should be unpacked as a geodesic net with empty boundary set (no unbalanced vertices). ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/fparsch/parsch_thesis.pdf))

If one wants the question to be fully self-contained, one should also recall the balancing condition from the paper's definition of geodesic net: at each non-boundary vertex, the sum of the incident unit tangent vectors is zero. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1904.00483))

The paper adopts a global convention that all geodesic nets under discussion are connected, so making connectedness explicit improves paper-faithfulness. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1904.00483))
refined_question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold M of dimension at least 3 admit a connected closed geodesic net modeled on the θ-graph, that is, a geodesic net with empty boundary set (so the balancing condition holds at every vertex) whose underlying graph has two vertices joined by three distinct edges?
justification: The draft is already aimed at the exact open problem in Section 2. In the surrounding paragraph, the paper introduces the θ-graph as the simplest example of a closed geodesic net not containing a non-trivial periodic geodesic, describing it as two vertices connected by three distinct edges/geodesics; immediately afterward it states Problem 2.0.3 in the dimension-≥3 setting. Definition 1.1.1 supplies the hidden balancing-condition content of the term "geodesic net," and the conventions right after that definition explain the connectedness convention. Because your draft already matches the scope and graph shape, the only real refinements are to make the paper's terminology and implicit conventions explicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1904.00483))
